Gil 22 EDGAR C. TENGKI Punong Barangay Barangay Damar, Damar Loop St., Damar Village, Quezon City Dear PB Tengki: This refers to your letter dated 20 February 2024 in relation to your request to review the practice of the Sangguniang Panlungsod (SP) and to correct the alleged common mistake of issuing either "Special Use Permit" or "Certificate of Exception". Per representation, the Sangguniang Barangay of Barangay Damar, Quezon City passed resolution No. 118, s. 2023, objecting on the proposed SP Resolution authorizing the issuance of a certificate of exception to Josephine Go to build a four (4) storey commercial / residential building, allowing deviation provided under City Ordinance No. SP-2502,s . 2016 or the Comprehensive Zoning Ordinance of 2016. Hence, you wrote a letter to Emmanuel D. Borromeo, City Director, DILG, QCFD, regarding this matter. Subsequently, Hon. Emmanuel D. Borromeo, in his response to your letter, stated that upon reading of City Ordinance No. SP-2502, there are items allowing exceptions and deviations from the previous provisions of the Zoning Ordinance. It is in this regard that he stressed that once an ordinance has undergone the procedural process for its enactment pursuant to Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991" (LGC), the same is considered valid unless declared otherwise by the courts, and this Department is bereft of authority to rule on the legality of the ordinance in question, as such is within the jurisdiction of the regular courts. Under this premise arose your request for this Office to issue an order reversing the opinion contained in Hon. Borromeo's letter, and to affirm the validity of Barangay Damar Resolution No. 118, s. 2023, and to enjoin all local government unis (LGUs) from giving exemptions to the enforcement of national laws, including, in this case, the National Building Code. At the outset, this Office would like to affirm the opinion of Emmanuel D. Borromeo, City Director, DILG, QCFD. While this Department exercises general supervision over local government units (LGUs), we have no authority to declare invalid any executive order issued by the local chief executives, ordinance and resolution passed by the local sanggunians, or any act committed by the members thereof which is alleged to be in violation of the LGC or "Matino, Mahusay, at Maaasahan" Trunkline: (02) 8876-3454

other applicable laws. Only the courts have the authority to do so upon initiation of the appropriate action for Declaratory Relief before the proper court, in accordance with Section I, Rule 63 of the Revised Rules of Court. Moreover, in our internal rulesl, the Department is proscribed to act on queries regarding presumptively valid acts, e.g., enacted ordinances, consummated acts that already enjoy the presumption of regularity on the part of the public officer concerned, and similar cases. Notwithstanding, while local government units enjoy local autonomy and are empowered to issue the necessary orders, resolutions, and enact ordinances, within their jurisdiction, however, it must, at all times, ensure that it does not contravene any statute and its orders, issuance, and policies are in harmony, and consistent with existing laws, and policies of the national government. Accordingly, if you believe that laws/statues are indeed violated, you may file a corresponding action before the appropriate forum. This opinion shall be without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY E UTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. TOR R. LLAMAS cretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairsq OUSELLÆJVRU/LLLS-LRALLD/rjki copy furnished: MARIA LOURDES L.
